results.summary: This design is a 2-to-4 binary decoder that takes two input bits and activates one of four outputs. It is intended to be used with a DIP switch for inputs and a 7-segment LED display to show which output is active. The documentation notes that due to tight timing, a certain input combination may light a different LED than expected, but otherwise it works as desired. The project is a simple educational combinational logic circuit implemented in Wokwi.

This design creates a moving circle effect on an 8-segment LED display using a series of D flip-flops. It requires an external seven-segment display to show the animation. The project is a simple educational example of sequential logic and shift register operation. The documentation is minimal and does not provide detailed testing instructions.

This project implements a frequency divider and some random logic, as indicated by its title and description. The documentation is essentially empty, providing no details on how it works, how to test it, or what external hardware is needed. It is a Wokwi design with a 10 kHz clock input. Without further information, the exact functionality cannot be determined.

This combinational circuit takes a 4-bit BCD input (A as MSB, D as LSB) and drives a 7-segment display to show numbers 1 through 9. It is tested by using DIP switches to set the input and observing the displayed digit. The design requires an external DIP switch and a seven-segment display. It is a simple educational project built in Wokwi.

This design debounces the two signals from a rotary encoder and outputs a clean clock and an up/down direction signal. It is intended to be connected to a rotary encoder, preferably one from an Arduino set, and the outputs can be used with a counter. The design is tested by connecting the encoder to the inputs and checking the outputs. It is a simple utility block for interfacing mechanical encoders with digital logic.

This project appears to implement some adders, as mentioned in the description, but the documentation is very sparse. It has 8 inputs and 8 outputs, and testing involves turning inputs 1-4 on and off. No external hardware is listed. The exact functionality and purpose are unclear due to the lack of detailed documentation.

This design is a hidden combination puzzle where the correct input sequence causes all LEDs to light up. It is tested by trying different input combinations. The project requires an LED display as external hardware. The documentation is minimal, providing only a brief description of the goal.

This project is extremely simple: pressing a button presumably lights an LED. The documentation is almost non-existent, with only 'Press the button' as the description. It has three inputs and no outputs listed, but external hardware includes an LED. The design is likely a basic introduction to digital input and output.

This design takes eight input signals, each corresponding to a number from 0 to 7, and displays that number on a 7-segment display. It is tested by following instructions in the info.yaml file. The project requires an external 7-segment display. The documentation is very brief, stating only that it 'just does' the described function.

This design displays the number 3 on a seven-segment display when switches 1, 2, and 3 are all turned on. It is tested by turning on those switches. The project requires an external seven-segment display. The documentation is minimal, providing only a brief description of the behavior.
